hard_gates.gate: G1 catches tenant leaks planted in p05's surface
hard_gates.evidence: Plant L10 (plants/L10-pooled-scratch-skip-total.patch) leaks and passes every G1 test. ListBinding.QueryAsync takes a per-query scratch object from an ObjectPool<ListPageScratch>, registered as a DI singleton in ListsModule. The scratch keeps a total keyed by list|search|filter with no tenant and is never cleared, and skip pages reuse it. All 38 G1 tests passed (plants/run-L10-g1-all.log, 2005 s), as did ProcessState, TenantSource and NonInterference (run-L10-structural.log). Live on a plant stack (plants/plant-live-L10.txt): gulfsteel page 1 of search 'a' has total 1004, alnoor page 1 has 3004, and gulfsteel skip=50 then shows 3004. The same happens for 'khalid' (28 vs 70) and language eq 'ar' (203 vs 640). The web client itself sends skip= when a user jumps (useListRows.ts:66). Two blind spots let it through. (1) ListAnswers judges first pages and keyset (after=) pages only and never sends skip; NonInterference never pages with skip either. (2) Process-state roots are product singletons and statics, and a singleton whose implementation type is a framework type (DefaultObjectPool<T>) holding product objects is never walked. Gates that held: L9, the same skip memo kept in AppDomain data, was caught by G1TenantSourceTests 'process-global' (run-L9-g1-rest.log), though ListAnswers, NonInterference and HttpIsolation all passed it (run-L9-g1.log). L6 from r4 (static Func memo in ListBinding<T>), re-planted by hand, is now caught by G1ProcessStateTests (run-L6-processstate-recheck.log), so r4's L6 gap stays fixed.

biggest_gap.title: Offset (skip) pages are judged by no gate, so a tenant-blind total memo in the list engine passes all of G1
biggest_gap.detail: Every later module registers its lists with p05 and relies on G1 to attack them automatically. The list engine has two paging modes, keyset (after=) and offset (skip=), and the client itself sends skip= when a user jumps through a long list. ListAnswers judges first pages and keyset pages only. NonInterference never pages with skip. A skip page whose total comes from state shared across tenants is therefore unseen whenever that state lives anywhere the structural gates miss. My plant L10 keeps it in a pooled scratch object: ObjectPool<ListPageScratch>, a DI singleton whose implementation is the framework's DefaultObjectPool<T>. The process-state gate only walks singletons whose implementation type is a product type, so it never reaches the object. The tenant-source scanner has no rule for object pools. Fixes: (a) in ListAnswers (and NonInterference), walk each query by offset as well: skip pages in lock step with the other tenant, with the total and groups of every skip page judged against the walked rows; (b) in process state, walk every singleton instance, framework implementation types included, down to the product objects it holds, or flag pools, caches and any singleton whose generic arguments are product types; (c) add object pools and IMemoryCache-like framework stores to the tenant-source 'process-global' rule.
biggest_gap.evidence: Apply gauntlet/evidence/p05-list-search/r5/plants/L10-pooled-scratch-skip-total.patch. Then `dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~Erp.Gates.Tests.G1` passes 38/38 (plants/run-L10-g1-all.log). Live on a stack with the plant (scripts/plant-live.mjs, plants/plant-live-L10.txt): GET /api/identity/users?take=50&search=a answers total 1004 to admin@gulfsteel and 3004 to admin@alnoor. Then gulfsteel's GET ...&skip=50 answers total 3004, which is alnoor's count. The same happens for search=khalid (28 vs 70) and filter language eq 'ar' (203 vs 640).

other_findings: G2 misses plant P5 on p05's own bulk endpoint. POST /api/identity/users/matching/active (b20cb59, p05 round 5) applies 'never change a user who holds a permission the caller lacks' only in its handler. With that check removed, all 29 G2 tests pass and a user manager deactivates an Administrator that the single-user route refuses with 403 (plants/plant-live-P5.txt). G2 needs an account-takeover check for every route that changes users selected by a search or filter, not just /users/{id}: a caller with exactly the endpoint's permission aims the search at a stronger user, and the stronger user must stay unchanged. The control on the real product holds (refusedBeyondOwn 1).

[route: p00-foundation] The process-state inspector (ProcessState.ContextOf/Roots) skips DI singletons whose implementation type is not in a product assembly. A framework container such as DefaultObjectPool<T>, or any framework singleton built over product types, can hold cross-tenant product state unseen. This weakness applies beyond lists.

[route: p03-identity] G2AccountTakeoverTests enumerates only endpoints under /api/identity/users/{ and /api/identity/roles/{, so set-based user changes (matching/active and any future bulk route) are outside its takeover check.
